title: Free-category resolution augmentation after adjoining an ordinary category
statement:
Let $O$ be a small set and let $A,C$ be small ordinary categories [def-nagata-category] with object set $O$. All functors considered below fix $O$. For categories on $O$, write $D*_O E$ for their coproduct among categories with object set $O$ and functors fixing $O$: its arrows are composable words of arrows from the two factors, modulo the composition and identity relations within each factor. Let $F$ be the free-category comonad on these categories. The category $FD$ has object set $O$ and one graph generator $[d]:x\to y$ for every nonidentity arrow $d:x\to y$ of $D$; its arrows are finite composable words of generators, including empty words as identities. For a functor $u:D\to E$, the functor $Fu:FD\to FE$ sends $[d]$ to $[u(d)]$ if $u(d)$ is nonidentity and to the identity otherwise. The counit $\epsilon_D:FD\to D$ composes a word; the comultiplication $\delta_D:FD\to F^2D$ sends $[d]$ to $[[d]]$. Define the augmented simplicial category $F_\bullet C\to C$ by $(F_\bullet C)_n=F^{n+1}C$, faces $d_i=F^i\epsilon F^{n-i}$ and degeneracies $s_i=F^i\delta F^{n-i}$ for $0\leq i\leq n$. Regard $A$ and $A*_O C$ as constant simplicial categories, and set $R_n=A*_O F^{n+1}C$, with operators identity on $A$ and the indicated operators on the other factor. For every $x,y\in O$, composition of the nested words induces a weak homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]
$$R_\bullet(x,y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{const}\bigl((A*_O C)(x,y)\bigr).$$
There is no freeness or cofibrancy hypothesis on $A$ or $C$.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories, Section 2.4 (free-category comonad), Section 2.5 (standard resolution), Proposition 2.6, and proof of Proposition 2.7(iii), printed pp.270-271, specialized to constant A and C. Read online, not archived locally. No Stacks tag states this enriched-category resolution comparison.

proof.text: The free-category construction on a category with object set $O$ is functorial: a map of categories sends each nonidentity generator to the corresponding generator, or to the identity when its image is an identity. Composition of words gives the counit $\epsilon$, and replacing each generator by its one-letter outer word gives the comultiplication $\delta$. The two comonad identities are checked on generators and then on words. Substituting these identities into $d_i=F^i\epsilon F^{n-i}$ and $s_i=F^i\delta F^{n-i}$ gives the simplicial identities, so $F_\bullet C\to C$ is an augmented simplicial category and the same operators, acting trivially on the $A$ factor, make $R_\bullet$ a simplicial object.

source.place: §2.4, equations defining the free-category comonad; §2.5, the displayed face and degeneracy formulas (printed pp.270–271).

proof.text: Fix $x,y\in O$ and write $X_n=(F^{n+1}C)(x,y)$ and $S=C(x,y)$. For any category $D$, define the map of its underlying reflexive graph $\gamma_D:D\to FD$ by $\gamma_D(1_x)=1_x$ and $\gamma_D(w)=[w]$ for a nonidentity arrow $w$. This is not asserted to be a functor. For every functor $v:D\to E$ it satisfies $Fv\,\gamma_D=\gamma_Ev$, including when $v(w)$ is an identity. Set $h_{-1}=\gamma_C$ and $h_n=\gamma_{F^{n+1}C}$ on these mapping sets. The counit gives $\varepsilon_0h_{-1}=1$ and $d_0h_n=1$. Since $d_1:F^2C\to FC$ is $F\epsilon_C$, naturality gives $d_1h_0=h_{-1}\varepsilon_0$. In higher degrees $d_{i+1}=F(d_i)$ and $s_{i+1}=F(s_i)$, so naturality gives $d_{i+1}h_{n+1}=h_nd_i$ and $s_{i+1}h_n=h_{n+1}s_i$ in precisely the ranges in [lem-coef-extra-degeneracy-contraction]. That node supplies a simplicial section and a homotopy to the identity. By [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] their realizations are a section and an ordinary homotopy inverse; consequently they induce inverse maps on components and all homotopy groups. Thus $X\to\operatorname{const}S$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Every $h_n$ and $h_{-1}$ fixes the identity arrow; this last property will also contract the identity boundaries of word spaces.

source.place: Proposition 2.6, printed p.270; explicit verification of its contracting homotopy, with realization justified by the cited cylinder lemma.

proof.text: For ordinary categories $A,D$ on $O$, reduce a composable word by deleting identity letters and replacing adjacent letters in the same factor by their composite. Each move strictly decreases length. The only overlapping moves involve three letters in one factor, or an identity next to a composition: associativity and the unit laws give a common further reduction in these cases; disjoint moves commute. Induction on the original word length then shows that two choices of first move have the same terminal reduced word, since their common reduct and both first reducts have smaller length. Hence every arrow of $A*_O D$ has a unique reduced word, alternating nonidentity letters from the two factors; the empty word represents an identity. This proves the normal-form assertion used below directly from the defining word relations, including factors with inverses or other composites equal to identities.

source.place: Section 1.4(iii), printed p.269; elementary normal-form argument for its alternating-word description.

proof.text: Put $X=F_\bullet C$ and $Y=\operatorname{const}C$. For $Z=X$ or $Y$, let $W_l(Z)(x,y)$ consist of the arrows of $(A*_O Z)(x,y)$ whose reduced words have total length at most $l$. Faces and degeneracies replace each letter by its image and then reduce, so cannot increase this length; thus these are simplicial subsets. Define $P_l(Z)(x,y)$, for $l\geq1$, as the disjoint union over object paths $x=x_0,\ldots,x_l=y$ and alternating strings of $A$ and $Z$ of the products of the following $l$ mapping spaces: at an $A$ slot use the constant set of nonidentity arrows $A(x_{j-1},x_j)$, and at a $Z$ slot use all of $Z(x_{j-1},x_j)$, including identities. Let $B_l(Z)\subseteq P_l(Z)$ be the union of loci where at least one $Z$ slot is an identity (possible only at equal endpoints). It is a simplicial subset. Multiplication sends $B_l(Z)$ to $W_{l-1}(Z)$ because deleting that identity decreases length and every subsequent reduction decreases it further. There is a degreewise pushout square with top row $B_l(Z)\hookrightarrow P_l(Z)$ and bottom row $W_{l-1}(Z)\hookrightarrow W_l(Z)$: outside $B_l(Z)$ every letter is nonidentity, so the normal form of Step 3 identifies these tuples bijectively with the reduced words of length exactly $l$; all boundary tuples are identified with their unique lower-length reduced word. These degreewise identifications commute with the simplicial operators just described. In particular the top map is a monomorphism. The augmentation induces a map between these squares for $X$ and $Y$, even when it sends a nonidentity $X$ arrow to an identity.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.7(iii), printed p.271; explicit word-length pushout construction expanding the omitted details. Construction and pushout verification are by the word normal form in Step 3.

proof.text: On $P_l(X)$ define degree-raising maps by applying the maps $h_n$ of Step 2 to every $X$ slot and keeping every $A$ letter, object path and alternating string fixed. Define the section of its augmentation to $P_l(Y)$ by applying $h_{-1}$ in every $C$ slot. All extra-degeneracy equations hold coordinate by coordinate, including products with no $X$ slots and empty summands. These maps restrict to $B_l(X)$ and a section from $B_l(Y)$ because each identity coordinate is fixed by $h_n$ and $h_{-1}$. The same equations therefore hold on this union of identity loci. Apply [lem-coef-extra-degeneracy-contraction] separately to these two augmented simplicial sets. The realization-cylinder statement [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] turns the resulting simplicial homotopies into ordinary homotopies, as in Step 2. We obtain weak homotopy equivalences $P_l(X)\to P_l(Y)$ and $B_l(X)\to B_l(Y)$. No contraction on reduced coproduct words is asserted: contractions are used only on the tuple spaces and their identity boundaries.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.7(iii), printed p.271, using the contraction of Proposition 2.6; explicit contraction of each attaching space and its identity boundary.

proof.text: The initial stage $W_0(X)(x,y)\to W_0(Y)(x,y)$ is an isomorphism: both are a singleton if $x=y$ and empty otherwise. Induct on $l$. In the two pushout squares of Step 4, the boundary inclusions $B_l(Z)\hookrightarrow P_l(Z)$ are monomorphisms; the boundary and tuple comparisons are weak homotopy equivalences by Step 5, and the lower-stage comparison is one by the induction hypothesis. The pushout assertion of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] gives the comparison at stage $l$. Every simplex of either coproduct is represented by a finite word, so the degreewise colimits over $l\in\mathbb N$ are exactly $(A*_O X)(x,y)$ and $(A*_O Y)(x,y)$. The filtered-colimit assertion of the same node now proves that their augmentation is a weak homotopy equivalence. This proves the required conclusion for every $x,y$. If $O$ is empty there are no pairs; identity-only factors and empty mapping spaces are already included in the construction. Neither the induction nor the contractions assume freeness or cofibrancy of $A$ or $C$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.7(iii), printed p.271; the omitted extension is supplied by the explicit pushout induction and the cited filtered-colimit theorem.
